source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. V (Montreuil)

1.title: Expositio capituli primi: Tobias ex tribu et civitate Nephthali
1.title_en: Exposition of the first chapter: Tobias of the tribe and city of Nephtali

paras.t: Hoc primo capitulo describitur conversatio virtuosa Tobiæ, præsertim in operibus misericordiæ.
paras.en: In this first chapter is described the virtuous manner of life of Tobias, above all in works of mercy.

paras.t: Tobias ex tribu et civitate Nephthali. Nephthali interdum est nomen unius duodecim Patriarcharum, filiorum Jacob patriarchæ, qui ex conjuge sua nomine Bala, ancilla Rachelis, genuit Dan et Nephthali, ut patet in Genesi. Interdum Nephthali sumitur pro tota tribu ex præfato Nephthali orta. Quandoque vero pro civitate Galilææ ad tribum Nephthali pertinente, ut aliqui dicunt. Verumtamen in libro Josue, ubi civitates tribus Nephthali exprimuntur, nulla sic appellatur; nec etiam primo Paralipomenon libro. Ideo istud videtur incertum aut falsum, nisi forsan aliqua urbium illarum, alio nomine dicta sit Nephthali, aut postea sit constructa. Fuit ergo Tobias ex tribu Nephthali patriarchæ, et ex civitate pertinente ad tribum Patriarchæ ejusdem; vel ex civitate nomine Nephthali. Quæ est in superioribus Galilææ, id est in locis et partibus eminentioribus, seu magis orientalibus provinciæ Galilææ. Circa quod aliqui dicunt, ideo esse dictum, In superioribus Galilææ, quoniam duplex est Galilæa, scilicet superior atque inferior, et quod Tobias fuit de Galilæa superiori. Sed juxta hoc (ut apparet) potius dictum fuisset, Quæ est in superiori Galilæa. Supra Naasson, id est juxta aut supra urbem Galilææ sic nominatam. Aliquando autem Naasson est proprium nomen viri: unde in Numeris filius Aminadab nomine Naasson, scribitur princeps tribus Juda fuisse. Post viam quæ ducit ad occidentem, in sinistro habens civitatem Sephet.
paras.en: [[1:1|Tobias of the tribe and city of Nephtali|Tobias ex tribu et civitate Nephthali]]. Nephthali is sometimes the name of one of the twelve Patriarchs, the sons of the patriarch Jacob, who of his wife named Bala, the handmaid of Rachel, begot Dan and Nephthali, as is plain in Genesis[[Gen 30:5||]] [the margin gives Gen. xxx, its verse numbers unreadable; the births of Dan and Nephthali are told at vv. 5–8]. Sometimes Nephthali is taken for the whole tribe sprung from the aforesaid Nephthali; and sometimes for a city of Galilee belonging to the tribe of Nephthali, as some say. Yet in the book of Josue, where the cities of the tribe of Nephthali are set out[[Jos 19:32||]] [the margin gives Josue xix, 32–39], none is so called; nor in the first book of Paralipomenon either[[1 Par 6:76||]]. Therefore this seems uncertain or false, unless perhaps one of those cities was called Nephthali by another name, or was built afterwards. Tobias, then, was of the tribe of the patriarch Nephthali, and of a city belonging to the tribe of that same Patriarch; or else of a city named Nephthali. [[1:1|which is in the upper parts of Galilee|Quæ est in superioribus Galilææ]], that is, in the higher and more eminent places and parts, or the more eastern ones, of the province of Galilee. On this some say that it is said [[1:1|in the upper parts of Galilee|In superioribus Galilææ]] because Galilee is twofold, namely upper and lower, and that Tobias was of upper Galilee. But on that view (as it seems) it would rather have been said, "Which is in upper Galilee." [[1:1|above Naasson|Supra Naasson]], that is, near or above a city of Galilee so named. But sometimes Naasson is the proper name of a man: whence in Numbers the son of Aminadab, named Naasson, is written to have been prince of the tribe of Juda[[Num 7:12||]] [the margin reads Num. vii, 12 or 13; he is called prince of Juda in so many words at Num 2:3 and 10:14]. [[1:1|beyond the way that leadeth to the west|Post viam quæ ducit ad occidentem]], [[1:1|having on the right hand the city of Sephet|in sinistro habens civitatem Sephet]] [the Latin has in sinistro, "on the left"; the Douay-Rheims reads "on the right hand"].

paras.t: Quum captus esset in diebus Salmanasar regis Assyriorum. Quarto Regum legitur, qualiter Teglathphalasar rex Assyriorum vastavit regnum decem tribuum, et multos ex eis cepit ac transtulit in Assyrios, tempore Phacee regis Israel, regnante in Juda Ozia rege, qui alio nomine dictus est Azarias. Et hæc vocatur prima captivitas decem tribuum. Postea Salmanasar rex Assyriorum, filius prædicti regis Assyrii, vastavit, cepit, et transtulit decem tribus, scilicet eos qui ex tribubus illis residui erant in terra promissionis. Et hæc vocatur secunda captivitas tribuum decem, quæ facta est sexto anno Ezechiæ regis Juda, et nono anno Osee regis Israel. In qua captivitate Tobias inter ceteros est abductus: non quod ipse captivari et transferri meruerit, sed quia in punitione justa iniquorum, interdum contingit et justos ac innocentes corporalibus pœnis involvi cum impiis, sicut per Ezechielem Dominus dixit Jerusalem: Occidam in te justum et impium. Sic enim Daniel cum sociis suis, atque Ezechiel a Chaldæis capti fuerunt. Quod tamen nec divinæ providentiæ, nec divinæ repugnat justitiæ. Justi enim et electi multipliciter in hac vita tribulantur, non solum pro culpis suis, sed etiam pro majori eorum profectu, et ut gloriosius coronentur, et ut exercitentur adversis, ac aliis in exemplum patientiæ proponantur, sicut et infra tangetur. Talia ergo adversa ordinat justus et supersapientissimus Deus suis electis in majus bonum.
paras.en: [[1:2|When he was made captive in the days of Salmanasar king of the Assyrians|Quum captus esset in diebus Salmanasar regis Assyriorum]]. In the fourth book of Kings we read how Teglathphalasar king of the Assyrians laid waste the kingdom of the ten tribes, and took many of them and carried them away into Assyria[[4 Kings 15:29||]], in the time of Phacee king of Israel, while Ozias, who by another name was called Azarias, reigned as king in Juda. And this is called the first captivity of the ten tribes. Afterwards Salmanasar king of the Assyrians, the son of the aforesaid Assyrian king, laid waste, took and carried away the ten tribes, namely those of those tribes who were left in the land of promise[[4 Kings 17:3||]] [the margin gives 4 Kings xvii, 3–6]. And this is called the second captivity of the ten tribes, which took place in the sixth year of Ezechias king of Juda, and the ninth year of Osee king of Israel. In this captivity Tobias was led away among the rest: not that he himself deserved to be made captive and carried away, but because in the just punishment of the wicked it sometimes happens that the just and innocent too are caught up in bodily punishments together with the ungodly, as the Lord said to Jerusalem through Ezechiel: I [[Ezech 21:3|will cut off in thee the just, and the wicked|Occidam in te justum et impium]]. For thus Daniel with his companions[[Dan 1:6||]], and Ezechiel[[Ezech 1:1||]], were taken captive by the Chaldeans. Yet this is not against the divine providence, nor against the divine justice. For the just and the elect are afflicted in many ways in this life[[Ps 33:20||]], not only for their own faults, but also for their greater progress, and that they may be crowned more gloriously, and that they may be exercised by adversities, and set before others as an example of patience, as will also be touched on below. Such adversities, then, the just and supremely wise God ordains for his elect unto a greater good.

paras.t: In captivitate tamen positus, id est in terra Assyriorum captivus habitans, puta in metropoli regni illius, hoc est in Ninive civitate: non quod fuerit ibi in nervo, aut cippo, aut carcere positus, sed jure vel violentia belli detentus: viam veritatis non deseruit, id est, observantiam legis divinæ, et cultum veri Dei non reliquit: imo permansit in veritate vitæ, in veritate doctrinæ, et in veritate justitiæ. Sicque in adversis exstitit constans, fidelis et patiens: in quo ejus relucet perfectio. Adversa etenim probant virum, juxta illud: Vasa figuli probat fornax, et homines justos tentatio tribulationis.
paras.en: [[1:2|even in his captivity|In captivitate tamen positus]], that is, dwelling as a captive in the land of the Assyrians, namely in the capital of that kingdom, that is, in the city of Ninive: not that he was put there in fetters, or the stocks, or prison, but held by the right or the force of war: [[1:2|forsook not the way of truth|viam veritatis non deseruit]], that is, did not leave off the keeping of the divine law and the worship of the true God; nay, he remained in the truth of life, in the truth of doctrine, and in the truth of justice. And so in adversity he stood constant, faithful and patient: in which his perfection shines out. For adversities prove a man, according to that saying: [[Ecclus 27:6|The furnace trieth the potter's vessels, and the trial of affliction just men|Vasa figuli probat fornax, et homines justos tentatio tribulationis]].

paras.t: Ita ut omnia quæ habere poterat, quotidie concaptivis fratribus qui erant ex ejus genere, impertiret, id est, filiis Israel secum captis condivideret et communicaret. Et per natos ex genere suo, possunt specialiter accipi nati ex tribu Nephthali: generaliter vero, quicumque exorti ex progenie et semine Jacob seu tribuum decem.
paras.en: [[1:3|But every day gave all he could get to his brethren his fellow captives, that were of his kindred|Ita ut omnia quæ habere poterat, quotidie concaptivis fratribus qui erant ex ejus genere, impertiret]], that is, shared out and imparted to the children of Israel taken captive with him. And by those born of his kindred may be understood specially those born of the tribe of Nephthali; but generally, whoever sprang from the stock and seed of Jacob, or of the ten tribes.

paras.t: Cumque esset junior omnibus in tribu Nephthali, id est unus juniorum, vel junior quibusdam singularum familiarum tribus illius, vel junior omnibus notabilibus personis tribus præfatæ, nihil tamen puerile gessit in opere, id est nihil contrarium laudabilibus moribus: sicque moribus ætatem transcendit, et maturitati, probitati, atque prudentiæ studuit ab ea ætate qua capax fuit discretionis, et in innocentia sua permansit, etiam inter dyscolos sceleratos atque idololatras vivens: quod fuit donum gratiæ specialis.
paras.en: [[1:4|And when he was younger than any of the tribe of Nephtali|Cumque esset junior omnibus in tribu Nephthali]], that is, one of the younger ones, or younger than some in each of the families of that tribe, or younger than all the notable persons of the aforesaid tribe, [[1:4|yet did he no childish thing in his work|nihil tamen puerile gessit in opere]], that is, nothing contrary to praiseworthy conduct; and so in conduct he went beyond his age, and gave himself to maturity, uprightness and prudence from the age at which he was capable of discretion, and remained in his innocence, though living among the froward, the wicked and idolaters: which was a gift of special grace.

paras.t: Denique quum omnes irent ad vitulos aureos, id est, quidam, imo et plurimi, de omnibus tribubus Israelitici regni, assidue tenderent ad adorandum vitulos aureos, quos Jeroboam fecerat per manus artificum, rex Israel, metuens, quod decem tribus redirent ad obedientiam Roboam filii Salomonis, si irent ad sacrificandum Deo in templo Jerusalem, prout tertio Regum libro recitatur; hic solus, id est præcipue præ ceteris, fugiebat consortia omnium illorum idololatrantium. Vel ideo dicitur solus, quia tam pauci de decem tribubus tempore illo recesserunt ab idololatria illa, quod aliorum respectu, quasi nulli videbantur.
paras.en: [[1:5|Moreover when all went to the golden calves|Denique quum omnes irent ad vitulos aureos]], that is, when some, nay very many, of all the tribes of the kingdom of Israel continually made their way to worship the golden calves, [[1:5|which Jeroboam king of Israel had made|quos Jeroboam fecerat per manus artificum, rex Israel]] by the hands of craftsmen, fearing that the ten tribes would return to the obedience of Roboam the son of Solomon if they went to sacrifice to God in the temple at Jerusalem, as is related in the third book of Kings[[3 Kings 12:28||]]: [[1:5|he alone|hic solus]], that is, he above the rest, [[1:5|fled the company of all|fugiebat consortia omnium]] those idolaters. Or he is said to be alone because so few of the ten tribes at that time withdrew from that idolatry that, in comparison with the others, they seemed as none.

paras.t: Et pergebat ad Jerusalem ad templum Domini, ad quod ivit occulte (ut communiter dicitur): quoniam reges Israel prohibuerunt id subditis suis, posueruntque in via et montibus quosdam ad observandum, an quis de regno Israel pergeret ad Jerusalem ad sacrificandum, ut dictum est super illud Osee: Laqueus facti estis speculationi, et sicut rete expansum super montem Thabor. Sed advertendum quod Osee rex Israel, cujus imperii nono anno captus est Tobias, dedit licentiam omni populo suo, eundi et sacrificandi Deo in templo Jerusalem, ut dicunt Hebræi. Unde super illud Osee, Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt, refert Hieronymus: Dicunt Hebræi, quod quamdiu reges decem tribuum et ipsæ tribus concorditer idola coluerunt, non fuerunt totaliter capti, quoniam idololatria populi aliqualiter excusabatur ex tyrannide regum, compellentium populum ad facinus tantum. Porro, Osee ultimus rex Israel jussit, ne vituli aurei tanto studio colerentur, contulitque licentiam plebi, ut irent et sacrificarent in templo Jerusalem: cui populus contradixit, sicque divisum fuit cor populi a corde regis. Propter quod nullam suæ idololatriæ excusationem habebant, et protinus capti sunt. Denique narratio ista videtur consonare Scripturis. Legitur namque quarto Regum, quod Osee rex fecit malum coram Domino, sed non sicut reges Israel qui ante eum fuerunt.
paras.en: [[1:6|And went to Jerusalem to the temple of the Lord|Et pergebat ad Jerusalem ad templum Domini]], to which he went secretly (as is commonly said), since the kings of Israel forbade this to their subjects, and set men on the road and on the mountains to watch whether anyone of the kingdom of Israel was going to Jerusalem to sacrifice, as was said on that text of Osee: [[Osee 5:1|you have been a snare to them whom you should have watched over|Laqueus facti estis speculationi]] [Latin speculationi, "to the place of watching": Denis takes it of these watchers], and as [[Osee 5:1|a net spread upon Thabor|rete expansum super montem Thabor]]. But note that Osee king of Israel, in the ninth year of whose reign Tobias was taken captive, gave leave to all his people to go and sacrifice to God in the temple at Jerusalem, as the Hebrews say. Hence on that text of Osee, [[Osee 10:2|Their heart is divided: now they shall perish|Divisum est cor eorum, nunc interibunt]], Jerome relates: "The Hebrews say that so long as the kings of the ten tribes and the tribes themselves worshipped idols with one accord, they were not wholly taken captive, since the idolatry of the people was in some measure excused by the tyranny of the kings, who drove the people to so great a crime. But Osee, the last king of Israel, commanded that the golden calves should not be worshipped with such zeal, and gave the common people leave to go and sacrifice in the temple at Jerusalem: the people opposed him, and so the heart of the people was divided from the heart of the king. For this reason they had no excuse for their idolatry, and were straightway taken captive." And indeed this account seems to agree with the Scriptures. For we read in the fourth book of Kings that king Osee [[4 Kings 17:2|did evil before the Lord: but not as the kings of Israel that had been before him|fecit malum coram Domino, sed non sicut reges Israel qui ante eum fuerunt]].

paras.t: Et ibi adorabat Dominum Deum Israel, quem utique adoravit quotidie, etiam extra templum, sed in solennitatibus legis, in quibus præceptum fuit ut sacrificia sua offerrent, et adorarent in templo, adoravit in eo, hoc est in festis Paschæ et Pentecostes ac Tabernaculorum, juxta illud Deuteronomii: Tribus vicibus per annum apparebit omne masculinum tuum in conspectu Domini Dei tui in loco quem elegerit: in solennitate Azymorum, et in solennitate Hebdomadarum, et in solennitate Tabernaculorum. Omnia primitiva sua, id est primitias frugum et animalium deputatas usibus sacerdotum, et decimas, quæ cedebant in sustentaculum Levitarum, prout in Levitico et Deuteronomio sæpe habetur, fideliter offerens Deo: ita ut in tertio anno proselytis et advenis ministraret omnem decimationem. Decimæ ordinatæ in sustentationem Levitarum, offerebantur quolibet anno: præter quas fuit et alia decima, quæ offerebatur semel in tribus annis, et cessit in usum pauperum, præsertim proselytorum, id est conversorum ad Judaismum, et advenarum seu peregrinorum. His ergo Tobias tertio anno exhibuit omnem decimationem, id est decimam partem omnium rerum suarum, de quibus secundum legem decima offerebatur. De his decimis in Deuteronomio et Numeris plenius legitur.
paras.en: [[1:6|and there adored the Lord God of Israel|Et ibi adorabat Dominum Deum Israel]]. Him indeed he adored daily, even outside the temple; but on the solemn feasts of the law, on which it was commanded that they should offer their sacrifices and adore in the temple, he adored in it: that is, on the feasts of the Pasch, of Pentecost and of Tabernacles, according to that of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 16:16|Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose: in the feast of unleavened bread, in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles|Tribus vicibus per annum apparebit omne masculinum tuum in conspectu Domini Dei tui in loco quem elegerit: in solennitate Azymorum, et in solennitate Hebdomadarum, et in solennitate Tabernaculorum]]. [[1:6|all his firstfruits|Omnia primitiva sua]], that is, the firstfruits of crops and of animals set apart for the use of the priests, [[1:6|and his tithes|et decimas]], which went to the support of the Levites, as is often found in Leviticus[[Lev 27:30||]] and Deuteronomy[[Deut 12:6||]], [[1:6|offering faithfully|fideliter offerens]] to God: [[1:7|So that in the third year he gave all his tithes to the proselytes, and strangers|ita ut in tertio anno proselytis et advenis ministraret omnem decimationem]]. The tithes appointed for the support of the Levites were offered every year; besides these there was also another tithe, which was offered once in three years, and went to the use of the poor, especially of proselytes, that is, converts to Judaism, and of strangers, that is, foreigners. To these, then, Tobias in the third year gave all his tithes, that is, the tenth part of all those goods of his of which a tithe was offered according to the law. Of these tithes more is read in Deuteronomy[[Deut 14:22||]] [the margin gives Deut. xiv, 22–28] and Numbers[[Num 18:24||]] [the margin gives Num. xviii, 24–32].

paras.t: Hæc et his similia puerulus observabat, id est adolescentulus, etiam nondum viginti annorum exsistens, infra quos pueri vocabantur, ut in Numeris habetur.
paras.en: [[1:8|These and such like things did he observe when but a boy|Hæc et his similia puerulus observabat]], that is, as a young lad, not yet twenty years of age, below which they were called boys, as is had in Numbers[[Num 1:3||]][[Ex 30:14||]] [the margin gives Num. i, 3 and a place in Exodus that reads like xii, 37; the rule of twenty years is at Exod 30:14].

paras.t: Quum vero factus fuisset vir, id est, postquam vicesimum attigit annum, accepit uxorem Annam de tribu sua: secundum illud Numerorum, Omnes viri ducent uxores de tribu et cognatione sua: quod potissime servabatur, dum feminæ successerunt in parentum hæreditate, ne si viris alterius tribus jungerentur connubio, sortium sequeretur confusio, hæreditate unius tribus ad tribum aliam transeunte. Alias non servabatur hoc semper: nam et David de tribu Juda, filiam Saul de tribu Benjamin duxit uxorem. Genuitque ex ea filium, nomen suum imponens ei, vocando eum Tobiam, quando circumcisus fuit, scilicet die octava. Hinc ineptum videtur, quod aliqui juniorem illum Tobiam nominant Tobi.
paras.en: [[1:9|But when he was a man|Quum vero factus fuisset vir]], that is, after he had reached his twentieth year, [[1:9|he took to wife Anna of his own tribe|accepit uxorem Annam de tribu sua]], according to that of Numbers: [[Num 36:7|all men shall marry wives of their own tribe and kindred|Omnes viri ducent uxores de tribu et cognatione sua]]. This was kept above all when women succeeded to their parents' inheritance, lest, if they were joined in marriage to men of another tribe, a confusion of the lots [that is, of the portions of land allotted to each tribe] should follow, the inheritance of one tribe passing to another tribe. Otherwise this was not always kept: for David too, of the tribe of Juda, took to wife the daughter of Saul, of the tribe of Benjamin[[1 Kings 18:27||]]. [[1:9|and had a son by her|Genuitque ex ea filium]], [[1:9|whom he called after his own name|nomen suum imponens ei]], calling him Tobias when he was circumcised, that is, on the eighth day. Hence it seems unfitting that some call the younger Tobias Tobi.

paras.t: Quem ab infantia, id est termino infantiæ, seu ab exordio quo uti cœpit discretione, timere Deum filiali timore docuit, et abstinere ab omni peccato, præsertim mortali, cui proprie competit ratio peccati, quum peccatum dicatur transgressio legis divinæ, et cœlestium inobedientia mandatorum: a quo peccato diu non abstinet, nisi qui et venialia cum diligentia vitat, quum venialia ad mortale disponant. Parentes autem filiis suis educationem, correctionem et informationem in moribus tenentur. Estque expediens, ut proles a pueritia sua sic informetur. Propter quod in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Non des filio potestatem in juventute sua; sed curva cervicem illius, et tunde latera ejus dum infans est. Hinc in Proverbiis inducitur: Adolescens juxta viam suam, etiam quum senuerit, non recedet ab ea.
paras.en: [[1:10|And from his infancy|Quem ab infantia]], that is, from the end of infancy, or from the time when he began to use discretion, he taught him [[1:10|to fear God|timere Deum]] with filial fear [that is, the fear of a son who dreads to offend his father, not the servile fear of punishment], [[1:10|and to abstain from all sin|et abstinere ab omni peccato]], especially mortal sin, to which the nature of sin properly belongs, since sin is called a transgression of the divine law and a disobedience to the heavenly commandments; and from such sin no one abstains for long unless he also carefully avoids venial sins, since venial sins dispose to mortal. Now parents are bound to give their children upbringing, correction and instruction in conduct; and it is expedient that offspring be so formed from their boyhood. Therefore it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 30:11|Give him not liberty in his youth|Non des filio potestatem in juventute sua]]; but [[Ecclus 30:12|bow down his neck|curva cervicem illius]], [[Ecclus 30:12|and beat his sides while he is a child|et tunde latera ejus dum infans est]]. Hence it is put in Proverbs: [[Prov 22:6|A young man according to his way, even when he is old, he will not depart from it|Adolescens juxta viam suam, etiam quum senuerit, non recedet ab ea]].

paras.t: Igitur quum per captivitatem devenisset cum uxore sua et filio in civitatem Niniven: quæ fuit metropolis Assyriorum, et constructa est ab Assur filio Sem, juxta illud Genesis, De terra illa egressus est Assur, et ædificavit Niniven: quæ (ut in Jona habetur) magna fuit itinere trium dierum: cum omni tribu sua, id est cum multis de singulis familiis tribus Nephthali. Juxta quem sensum subjungitur: et omnes ederent ex cibis gentilium, prohibitis in lege, prout in Levitico legitur; iste custodivit animam suam a transgressione legis, et nunquam contaminatus est in escis eorum, id est, illicita non comedit. Juxta quem modum apud Danielem asseritur: Proposuerat Daniel in corde suo, ne pollueretur de mensa regis, neque de vino potus ejus.
paras.en: [[1:11|And when by the captivity he with his wife and his son|Igitur quum per captivitatem devenisset cum uxore sua et filio]] [[1:11|was come to the city of Ninive|in civitatem Niniven]]: which was the capital of the Assyrians, and was built by Assur the son of Sem, according to that of Genesis: [[Gen 10:11|Out of that land came forth Assur, and built Ninive|De terra illa egressus est Assur, et ædificavit Niniven]]; which (as is had in Jonas) was [[Jon 3:3|a great city of three days' journey|magna fuit itinere trium dierum]]; [[1:11|and all his tribe|cum omni tribu sua]], that is, with many of each of the families of the tribe of Nephthali. In keeping with this sense it is added: [[1:12|When all ate of the meats of the Gentiles|omnes ederent ex cibis gentilium]], which were forbidden in the law, as is read in Leviticus[[Lev 11:1||]], [[1:12|he kept his soul|iste custodivit animam suam]] from transgressing the law, [[1:12|and never was defiled with their meats|et nunquam contaminatus est in escis eorum]], that is, he did not eat unlawful things. In the same way it is said of Daniel: [[Dan 1:8|Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not be defiled with the king's table, nor with the wine which he drank|Proposuerat Daniel in corde suo, ne pollueretur de mensa regis, neque de vino potus ejus]].

paras.t: Et quoniam memor fuit Domini in toto corde suo, non solum ad sciendum, sed item ad faciendum ac adimplendum divina præcepta, juxta id Psalmi: Et memores sunt mandatorum ipsius, ad faciendum ea. Itaque memor fuit Dei assidue atque stabiliter, attendens jugiter divinæ majestatis præsentiam, secundum illud in Psalmo: Providebam Dominum in conspectu meo semper. Et: Oculi mei semper ad Dominum. Sicque cum sancto Job dicere potuit: Considerans Deum, timore sollicitor. Dedit illi Deus gratiam in conspectu Salmanasar regis, cujus cor Deus inclinavit ad favendum Tobiæ propter ipsius virtutes. Nempe ut Salomon ait, Cor regis in manu Domini est; quocumque voluerit, inclinabit illud. Qui rursus fatetur: Qui diligit cordis munditiam, amicum habebit regem. Et dedit ei potestatem quocumque vellet ire, habens ipse Tobias libertatem faciendi quæcumque vellet facere, quæ tamen non derogarent honori regis, et cultui Creatoris. Talem quoque libertatem dedit Nabuzardan, ex commissione Nabuchodonosor, Jeremiæ.
paras.en: [[1:13|And because he was mindful of the Lord with all his heart|Et quoniam memor fuit Domini in toto corde suo]], not only so as to know the divine precepts but also to do and fulfil them, according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 102:18|And are mindful of his commandments to do them|Et memores sunt mandatorum ipsius, ad faciendum ea]]. Thus he was mindful of God constantly and steadfastly, attending unceasingly to the presence of the divine majesty, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 15:8|I set the Lord always in my sight|Providebam Dominum in conspectu meo semper]]. And: [[Ps 24:15|My eyes are ever towards the Lord|Oculi mei semper ad Dominum]]. And so with holy Job he could say: [[Job 23:15|when I consider him, I am made pensive with fear|Considerans Deum, timore sollicitor]]. [[1:13|God gave him favour in the sight of Salmanasar the king|Dedit illi Deus gratiam in conspectu Salmanasar regis]], whose heart God inclined to favour Tobias for his virtues. For, as Solomon says, [[Prov 21:1|the heart of the king is in the hand of the Lord: whithersoever he will, he shall turn it|Cor regis in manu Domini est; quocumque voluerit, inclinabit illud]]. And again he declares: [[Prov 22:11|He that loveth cleanness of heart|Qui diligit cordis munditiam]], [[Prov 22:11|shall have the king for his friend|amicum habebit regem]]. [[1:14|And he gave him leave to go whithersoever he would|Et dedit ei potestatem quocumque vellet ire]], Tobias himself having [[1:14|liberty to do|libertatem faciendi]] whatever he wished to do, so long as it did not detract from the honour of the king and the worship of the Creator. Such liberty too did Nabuzardan give to Jeremias, by commission of Nabuchodonosor[[Jer 39:11||]] [the margin gives Jer. xxxix, 11–14].

paras.t: Pergebat ergo per omnes qui erant in captivitate de populo suo, et monita salutis dabat eis, ut scilicet captivitatem suam æquanimiter tolerarent, et in Dei cultu persisterent. Et sicut in Scholastica historia additur, Contribules suos non custodientes se, graviter arguebat.
paras.en: [[1:15|He therefore went to all that were in captivity|Pergebat ergo per omnes qui erant in captivitate]] of his people, [[1:15|and gave them wholesome admonitions|et monita salutis dabat eis]], namely that they should bear their captivity with an even mind and persevere in the worship of God. And, as is added in the Scholastic History [of Peter Comestor], he rebuked severely those of his tribe who did not keep themselves.

paras.t: Quum autem venisset in Rages civitatem Medorum, quibus tunc imperabant Assyrii: unde quarto Regum narratur rex Assyriorum collocasse captivos ex Israel in civitatibus Medorum; et ex his quibus honoratus fuerat a rege Salmanasar, puta ex munusculis sibi a rege collatis: qui honoravit Tobiam dono libertatis præfatæ atque pecuniæ, quemadmodum et de Jeremia legitur princeps militiæ Chaldæorum dedisse munuscula Jeremiæ; imo secundum Josephum, pretiosa munuscula dedit Prophetæ; habuisset decem talenta argenti; et quum in multa turba generis sui Gabelum egentem videret, qui erat ex tribu ejus: cum quo vidit et multos ex captis Israelitis egentes; sub chirographo dedit illi memoratum pondus argenti, id est, pecuniam illam concessit Gabelo sub cautione et chirographo de persolutione.
paras.en: [[1:16|And when he was come to Rages a city of the Medes|Quum autem venisset in Rages civitatem Medorum]], over whom the Assyrians then ruled (whence it is told in the fourth book of Kings that the king of the Assyrians placed the captives from Israel in the cities of the Medes[[4 Kings 17:6||]]), [[1:16|of that with which he had been honoured by the king|et ex his quibus honoratus fuerat a rege]] Salmanasar, that is, from the little gifts bestowed on him by the king, who honoured Tobias with the gift of the aforesaid liberty and with money, just as we read too of Jeremias that the captain of the soldiers of the Chaldeans gave presents to Jeremias[[Jer 40:5||]] (nay, according to Josephus, he gave the Prophet precious presents), [[1:16|and had ten talents of silver|habuisset decem talenta argenti]]; [[1:17|And when amongst a great multitude of his kindred, he saw Gabelus in want|et quum in multa turba generis sui Gabelum egentem videret]], [[1:17|who was one of his tribe|qui erat ex tribu ejus]] (and with him he saw many of the captive Israelites also in want), [[1:17|taking a note of his hand he gave him the aforesaid sum of money|sub chirographo dedit illi memoratum pondus argenti]]: that is, he lent that money to Gabelus under a bond and a note of hand for its repayment.

paras.t: Post multum vero temporis, mortuo Salmanasar, cujus vitam Deus prolongavit propter pietatem suam Tobiæ exhibitam, quum regnaret Sennacherib filius ejus: illis quippe temporibus Assyrii monarchiam tenebant; et filios Israel exosos haberet, præsertim percusso ejus exercitu ab angelo in regno Juda, ut paulo post in littera recitatur, et quarto Regum describitur; Tobias pergebat per omnem cognationem suam: quia cognatis, ceteris paribus, magis est succurrendum, sicut et magis sunt diligendi; et consolabatur eos verbis et beneficiis, sicut subjungitur: dividebatque unicuique prout poterat de facultatibus suis, etc.
paras.en: [[1:18|But after a long time|Post multum vero temporis]], [[1:18|Salmanasar the king being dead|mortuo Salmanasar]] (whose life God prolonged for the kindness he showed to Tobias), [[1:18|when Sennacherib his son, who reigned in his place|quum regnaret Sennacherib filius ejus]] (for in those times the Assyrians held the monarchy), [[1:18|had a hatred for the children of Israel|et filios Israel exosos haberet]], above all after his army had been struck by the angel in the kingdom of Juda, as is told a little later in the text, and described in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 19:35||]][[Is 37:36||]]: [[1:19|Tobias|Tobias]] [[1:19|went among all his kindred|pergebat per omnem cognationem suam]], since kinsfolk, other things being equal, are rather to be helped, as they are also rather to be loved; [[1:19|and comforted them|et consolabatur eos]] with words and good deeds, as is added: [[1:19|and distributed to every one as he was able, out of his goods|dividebatque unicuique prout poterat de facultatibus suis]], etc.

paras.t: At ubi nuntiatum est regi Sennacherib, quod Tobias tot opera misericordiæ exhiberet filiis Israel desolatis, jussit eum occidi, et tulit, id est abstulit, omnem substantiam ejus. Tobias vero cum filio suo et uxore fugiens, quia præavisatus fuit ab aliquo de suo periculo, nudus latuit, id est, rebus suis spoliatus abscondit se, quia multi diligebant eum, non solum ex filiis Israel, sed ex Assyriis quoque, quoniam erat totus mansuetus, pius, liberalis, pacificus, humilis et modestus.
paras.en: [[1:22|But when it was told the king|At ubi nuntiatum est regi]] Sennacherib that Tobias was showing so many works of mercy to the desolate children of Israel, [[1:22|he commanded him to be slain|jussit eum occidi]], [[1:22|and took away|et tulit]], that is, carried off [Latin tulit, "took", which Denis explains by abstulit, "took away"], [[1:22|all his substance|omnem substantiam ejus]]. [[1:23|But Tobias fleeing naked away with his son and with his wife|Tobias vero cum filio suo et uxore fugiens]], because he had been forewarned of his danger by someone, [[1:23|lay concealed|nudus latuit]] [Latin nudus latuit, "lay hidden naked"], that is, stripped of his goods, hid himself, [[1:23|for many loved him|quia multi diligebant eum]], not only of the children of Israel but of the Assyrians too, since he was wholly gentle, kind, generous, peaceable, humble and modest.

paras.t: Post dies vero quadraginta quinque occiderunt regem filii ejus. De qua occisione habetur quarto Regum, et secundo Paralipomenon, atque in Isaia; sed de numero horum dierum hic solum fit mentio. Et potest intelligi, quod vel post reditum ejus a regno Juda, et ingressum in Niniven, vel post præceptum quo sic jussit tractari Tobiam, fluxerunt dies hi quadraginta quinque. Cur autem filii occiderunt regem tam impium, dictum est super libros Regum et Isaiam. Nempe (ut aliqui dicunt) ordinavit filium suum juniorem sibi in regno suo succedere: propter quod indignati filii seniores, eum interfecerunt. Alii vero affirmant, quod populus suus indignabatur ei propter occisos in terra Juda, et voluit eum occidere: propter quod confugit in templum dei sui Nesroch, invocans eum, et promittens quod immolaret ei filios suos seniores, si eriperet eum de instanti periculo: quo cognito, filii sui seniores eum interemerunt.
paras.en: [[1:24|But after forty-five days|Post dies vero quadraginta quinque]], [[1:24|the king was killed by his own sons|occiderunt regem filii ejus]]. Of this slaying an account is had in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 19:37||]], in the second of Paralipomenon[[2 Par 32:21||]], and in Isaias[[Is 37:38||]]; but the number of these days is mentioned here only. And it can be understood that these forty-five days ran either from his return from the kingdom of Juda and his entry into Ninive, or from the command by which he ordered Tobias to be so treated. Why his sons slew so impious a king has been told on the books of Kings and on Isaias. For (as some say) he had appointed his younger son to succeed him in his kingdom, at which his elder sons were angered and slew him. But others affirm that his people were angry with him because of those slain in the land of Juda, and wished to kill him: on which account he fled into the temple of his god Nesroch[[Is 37:38||]], calling upon him and promising that he would sacrifice his elder sons to him if he would rescue him from the danger at hand; and his elder sons, learning of this, killed him.

paras.t: Et reversus est Tobias ad domum suam, omnisque facultas ejus restituta est ei, ex præcepto Asarhaddon, qui patri suo Sennacherib in regno successit, et pietatem in Tobiam exercuit, cognitis ejus virtutibus; et Deo sic ordinante, qui tempore tribulationis et tentationis misericorditer adest, nec permittit hominem supra illud quod potest tentari, sed facit cum tentatione proventum, et in ea virtutem victoriamque largitur.
paras.en: [[1:25|And Tobias returned to his house|Et reversus est Tobias ad domum suam]], [[1:25|and all his substance was restored to him|omnisque facultas ejus restituta est ei]], by order of Asarhaddon, who succeeded his father Sennacherib in the kingdom[[4 Kings 19:37||]][[Is 37:38||]] and showed kindness to Tobias, having come to know his virtues; and by the ordering of God, who is mercifully at hand in the time of tribulation and temptation, and does not suffer a man to be tempted above that which he is able, but makes [[1 Cor 10:13|with temptation issue|cum tentatione proventum]], and in it bestows strength and victory.

paras.t: Præterea allegorice Tobias Christum designat: de quo loquitur Jeremias, Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris; qui in omni ac summa pietate et innocentia vixit, et fructuosissimus mansit ab incarnationis exordio usque ad spiritus emissionem; qui duxit uxorem Ecclesiam, ex qua per prædicationem et Baptismum genuit filium unum, videlicet populum christianum in una fide et lege communicantem, cui imposuit nomen suum, quia a Christo Christianus vocatur. Denique Judæis in potestatem Romanorum redactis, atque ab invisibilibus hostibus gravissime captis, Christus pertransiit universos, consolando, docendo, reficiendo, miracula peragendo, quemadmodum sacratissimus ait princeps apostolici ordinis: Verbum misit Deus filiis Israel, annuntians pacem per Jesum Christum, qui pertransiit benefaciendo et sanando omnes oppressos a diabolo. Quumque Sennacherib, id est, persecutores et tyranni, odirent et persequerentur populum christianum ubique terrarum, Christus corda fidelium invisibiliter gratiosissime visitavit, consolabatur, refecit; ac tandem persecutoribus Ecclesiæ deficientibus ac deletis, Christus pacem dedit fidelibus, et restituta sunt ei in populo suo, quæ increduli abstulerunt membris et famulis Salvatoris.
paras.en: Moreover, allegorically Tobias signifies Christ, of whom Jeremias speaks: [[Lam 4:20|The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, is taken in our sins|Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris]]; who lived in all and the highest piety and innocence, and remained most fruitful from the beginning of his incarnation until he gave up his spirit; who took to wife the Church, of whom, through preaching and Baptism, he begot one son, namely the Christian people, sharing in one faith and law, on whom he laid his own name, since from Christ one is called a Christian. Then, when the Jews had been brought under the power of the Romans, and had been most grievously taken captive by invisible enemies, Christ went among them all, consoling, teaching, refreshing, working miracles, as the most holy prince of the apostolic order says: [[Acts 10:36|God sent the word to the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ|Verbum misit Deus filiis Israel, annuntians pacem per Jesum Christum]], [[Acts 10:38|who went about doing good and healing all that were oppressed by the devil|qui pertransiit benefaciendo et sanando omnes oppressos a diabolo]]. And when Sennacherib, that is, persecutors and tyrants, hated and persecuted the Christian people throughout the world, Christ invisibly and most graciously visited, consoled and refreshed the hearts of the faithful; and at length, when the persecutors of the Church had failed and been destroyed, Christ gave peace to the faithful, and there were restored to him in his people the things that the unbelievers had taken away from the members and servants of the Saviour.

paras.t: Tropologice, instruuntur ex isto capitulo universi fideles, ut in prosperis et adversis constanter adhæreant Deo, atque misericordiæ actibus toto corde consistant intenti, patientiam quoque in omni adversitate insuperabiliter amplectantur, etiam dato quod adversa non meruerint sustinere. Insuper sobolem suam ab infantia diligenter in omni informent virtute, præsertim in Dei timore ac moribus, non in vanitate, pompa et trufis, sicut nunc, proh dolor! faciunt multi.
paras.en: Tropologically [that is, in the moral sense], all the faithful are taught by this chapter to cleave to God constantly in prosperity and in adversity, and to be intent with their whole heart on works of mercy, and to embrace patience unconquerably in every adversity, even granted that they have not deserved to suffer adversities; and further, to form their offspring carefully from infancy in every virtue, especially in the fear of God and in good conduct, not in vanity, pomp and trifles, as, alas! many now do.

4.title: Elucidatio capituli quarti: Igitur quum Tobias putaret orationem suam exaudiri
4.title_en: Explanation of the fourth chapter: Therefore when Tobias thought that his prayer was heard

paras.t: Recitantur hic moralissima ac saluberrima documenta, quibus senior Tobias filium suum, et per eum universos instruxit fideles. Igitur quum Tobias putaret orationem suam exaudiri a Deo, ut mori potuisset, hoc est quoad hoc, quod cito (prout petiit) moreretur. Qualiter autem fuerit ejus oratio exaudita, patuit in præcedentis expositione capituli. Vocavit ad se Tobiam filium suum, dixitque ei: Audi, fili mi, verba oris mei, et ea in corde tuo quasi fundamentum construe, hoc est, firmissime ea imprime tuæ memoriæ. Consueverunt autem sancti patres, emigraturi de sæculo isto, sobolem suam salubriter exhortari, benedicere, informare, ut patet in Genesi de Jacob, et primo Paralipomenon de David. Sic et Christus post cœnam novissimam, passione sua instante, suos discipulos copiosissime informavit.
paras.en: Here are set out most moral and wholesome teachings, with which the elder Tobias instructed his son, and through him all the faithful. [[4:1|Therefore when Tobias thought that his prayer was heard|Igitur quum Tobias putaret orationem suam exaudiri]] by God [[4:1|that he might die|ut mori potuisset]]: that is, as regards this, that he should die soon (as he had asked). How his prayer was heard was shown in the explanation of the preceding chapter[[Tob 3:24||]] [the margin here is hard to read, apparently citing Tob. iii]. [[4:1|he called to him Tobias his son|Vocavit ad se Tobiam filium suum]], [[4:2|And said to him|dixitque ei]]: [[4:2|Hear, my son, the words of my mouth, and lay them as a foundation in thy heart|Audi, fili mi, verba oris mei, et ea in corde tuo quasi fundamentum construe]], that is, impress them most firmly on thy memory. Now the holy fathers, when about to depart from this world, were wont to exhort their offspring for their salvation, to bless them and instruct them, as is plain in Genesis of Jacob[[Gen 49:1||]], and in the first book of Paralipomenon of David[[1 Par 28:1||]]. So too Christ, after the last supper, with his passion at hand, instructed his disciples most fully[[John 13:1||]] [the margin gives John xiii–xvii].

paras.t: Quum acceperit Deus animam meam, separando eam a corpore, et in sinu Abrahæ eam ponendo, eamque (ut spero) misericorditer amplectendo, corpus meum sepeli, secundum quod ego sollicitus fui aliorum exstincta corpora sepelire, sciens quod in die resurgent novissimo. Sicque committimus ea terræ tanquam deposita quædam quæ suo tempore resumemus. Et honorem habebis, id est exhibebis, matri tuæ omnibus diebus vitæ ejus. Proles namque tenetur parentibus obedientiam et reverentiam, atque si indiguerint, necessariorum procurationem: a quibus beneficia tanta suscepit. Hinc subditur: Memor enim debes esse, quæ et quanta pericula passa sit propter te in utero suo: præsertim in partu, quo dolor, tremor, mœror, pressura, angustia, occupant et adimplent parturientem.
paras.en: [[4:3|When God shall take my soul|Quum acceperit Deus animam meam]], by separating it from the body, and placing it in the bosom of Abraham[[Luke 16:23||]], and (as I hope) mercifully embracing it, [[4:3|thou shalt bury my body|corpus meum sepeli]], even as I was careful to bury the lifeless bodies of others, knowing that they will rise again on the last day. And so we commit them to the earth as deposits which we shall take up again in their time. [[4:3|and thou shalt honour|Et honorem habebis]], that is, show honour to, [[4:3|thy mother all the days of her life|matri tuæ omnibus diebus vitæ ejus]]. For offspring is bound to give its parents obedience and reverence, and, if they are in need, to provide them with necessaries, since it has received such great benefits from them. Hence it is added: [[4:4|For thou must be mindful what and how great perils she suffered for thee in her womb|Memor enim debes esse, quæ et quanta pericula passa sit propter te in utero suo]]: above all in childbirth, when pain, trembling, grief, distress and anguish seize and fill the woman in labour.

paras.t: Quum autem et ipsa compleverit tempus vitæ suæ, sepelias eam circa me: ut quorum unus fuit lectus, unus sit tumulus, atque ut simul salubriter resurgamus, et qui conjuncti eramus in vita, non separemur post mortem. In his innotescunt patientia atque justitia venerandi Tobiæ, qui non obstante quod tam acriter et injuste fuit derisus a conjuge, ut patuit, tam diligenter commisit filio suo de cura illius.
paras.en: [[4:5|And when she also shall have ended the time of her life|Quum autem et ipsa compleverit tempus vitæ suæ]], [[4:5|bury her by me|sepelias eam circa me]]: so that those who had one bed may have one tomb, and that we may rise again together unto salvation, and we who were joined in life may not be parted after death. In these words the patience and justice of the venerable Tobias come to light: although he had been so bitterly and unjustly derided by his wife, as was shown[[Tob 2:22||]], he so carefully charged his son with her care.

paras.t: Omnibus autem diebus vitæ tuæ in mente habeto Deum, ad minus per habitum fidei, spei et caritatis, et quantum fieri potest per actus earumdem ac aliarum virtutum, pensando jugiter præsentiam Dei, implendoque illud Psalmographi, Meditatio cordis mei in conspectu tuo semper; et, Oculi mei semper ad Dominum. Et cave ne aliquando peccato consentias. Hoc est quod ait Apostolus: Nolite locum dare diabolo. Et prætermittas præcepta Dei, id est, cave ne negligas ea implere. Ideo in Ecclesiastico habetur: Salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate. A qua qualiter sit discedendum, tangitur in eodem, quum dicitur: Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccata.
paras.en: [[4:6|And all the days of thy life have God in thy mind|Omnibus autem diebus vitæ tuæ in mente habeto Deum]], at least by the habit of faith, hope and charity, and as far as can be, by the acts of these and of the other virtues, constantly weighing the presence of God, and fulfilling that word of the Psalmist, [[Ps 18:15|the meditation of my heart always in thy sight|Meditatio cordis mei in conspectu tuo semper]]; and, [[Ps 24:15|My eyes are ever towards the Lord|Oculi mei semper ad Dominum]]. [[4:6|and take heed thou never consent to sin|Et cave ne aliquando peccato consentias]]. This is what the Apostle says: [[Eph 4:27|Give not place to the devil|Nolite locum dare diabolo]]. [[4:6|nor transgress the commandments of the Lord|Et prætermittas præcepta Dei]], that is, take care not to neglect to fulfil them. Therefore it is said in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 35:2|It is a wholesome sacrifice to take heed to the commandments, and to depart from all iniquity|Salutare sacrificium est, attendere mandatis, et discedere ab omni iniquitate]]. How one must depart from it is touched on in the same book, where it is said: [[Ecclus 21:2|Flee from sins as from the face of a serpent|Quasi a facie colubri fuge peccata]].

paras.t: Insuper, quo Tobias actibus misericordiæ excellentius fuit intentus, eo ad ipsos efficacius ferventiusque hortatur, addendo: Ex substantia tua fac eleemosynam, et noli avertere faciem tuam ab ullo paupere te rogante, quin ad minus pie adspicias eum, ut consoleris verbo aut signo, si non habes corporale subsidium quod impendas. Ita enim fiet, ut nec a te avertatur facies Domini, id est divinæ pietatis respectus. Beati enim misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur. Et quanto quis proximis fuerit propter Deum benignior, eo Omnipotens gratiosior erit ei. Quomodo potueris, ita esto misericors, hoc est compassivus atque subveniens: sicut consequenter exponitur. Si multum tibi fuerit, abundanter tribue unicuique partem; si exiguum tibi fuerit, etiam exiguum libenter impertiri stude cum liberali affectu. Deus etenim magis pensat affectum, quam donum; et magis perpendit ex quanto, quam quantum. Ideo de paupercula mittente in gazophylacium duo minuta, dixit Salvator: Quia hæc vidua plus omnibus misit.
paras.en: Moreover, the more excellently Tobias was intent on works of mercy, the more effectively and fervently he exhorts to them, adding: [[4:7|Give alms out of thy substance|Ex substantia tua fac eleemosynam]], [[4:7|and turn not away thy face from any poor person|et noli avertere faciem tuam ab ullo paupere]] who asks of thee, but at least look kindly on him, so as to comfort him by word or sign, if thou hast no bodily help to bestow. [[4:7|for so it shall come to pass that the face of the Lord shall not be turned from thee|Ita enim fiet, ut nec a te avertatur facies Domini]], that is, the regard of the divine mercy. [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy|Beati enim misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur]]. And the kinder anyone is to his neighbours for God's sake, the more gracious the Almighty will be to him. [[4:8|According to thy ability be merciful|Quomodo potueris, ita esto misericors]], that is, compassionate and helping, as is set out next. [[4:9|If thou have much give abundantly|Si multum tibi fuerit, abundanter tribue]] to each a share; [[4:9|if thou have little, take care even so to bestow willingly a little|si exiguum tibi fuerit, etiam exiguum libenter impertiri stude]] with a generous heart. For God weighs the affection more than the gift, and considers more from how much than how much [that is, how much the giver had to give from, rather than the size of the gift]. Therefore of the poor widow casting two mites into the treasury, the Saviour said: [[Mark 12:43|this poor widow hath cast in more than all|hæc vidua plus omnibus misit]].

paras.t: Præmium enim bonum tibi thesaurisas, hoc est, acquiris et reponis: quod invenies in die necessitatis, id est mortis et judicii tui particularis ac universalis, et item in purgatorii pœnis, in quibus vivorum suffragia tantum prosunt, quantum defuncti hic meruerunt ut eis prodesse possint, hoc est, quo misericordiores fuerint. Hinc teste Ambrosio, Summa christianæ religionis in caritate et pietate consistit. Augustinus quoque asserit: Sola misericordia comes est defunctorum. Unde testatur Psalmista: Beatus qui intelligit super egenum et pauperem; in die mala liberabit eum Dominus.
paras.en: [[4:10|For thus thou storest up to thyself a good reward|Præmium enim bonum tibi thesaurisas]], that is, thou gainest and layest up, which thou wilt find [[4:10|for the day of necessity|in die necessitatis]]: that is, of death and of thy judgement, particular and universal, and likewise in the pains of purgatory, in which the suffrages of the living avail as much as the departed deserved here that they should avail them, that is, the more merciful they were. Hence, as Ambrose witnesses, the sum of the Christian religion consists in charity and loving-kindness. Augustine also asserts: Mercy alone is the companion of the dead. Whence the Psalmist testifies: [[Ps 40:2|Blessed is he that understandeth concerning the needy and the poor: the Lord will deliver him in the evil day|Beatus qui intelligit super egenum et pauperem; in die mala liberabit eum Dominus]].

paras.t: Quoniam eleemosyna ab omni peccato et a morte infernalis miseriæ liberat, dummodo fiat ex caritate et virtute misericordiæ; et non patietur animam ire in tenebras Acherontis. Et dato quod fiat extra caritatem, frequenter tamen de congruo gratiam promeretur, et intercessione ac meritis eorum quibus impenditur, gratia conversionis frequenter eleemosynariis datur. Hinc in Evangelio Dominus loquitur: Quod superest, date eleemosynam, et ecce omnia munda sunt vobis. Itemque: Facite vobis amicos de mammona iniquitatis, ut quum defeceritis, recipiant vos in æterna tabernacula. Fiducia magna, hoc est causa magnæ fiduciæ, erit coram summo Deo eleemosyna tam corporalis quam spiritualis, omnibus facientibus eam. De operibus quippe misericordiæ perhibet Christus se disceptaturum in die judicii, misericordibusque dicturum: Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum.
paras.en: [[4:11|For alms deliver from all sin, and from death|Quoniam eleemosyna ab omni peccato et a morte]] of hellish misery, provided it be done out of charity and the virtue of mercy; [[4:11|and will not suffer the soul to go into darkness|et non patietur animam ire in tenebras]] of Acheron. And granted that it be done outside charity, yet it often merits grace de congruo [that is, by a certain fittingness, not as a strict due], and through the intercession and merits of those on whom it is bestowed, the grace of conversion is often given to almsgivers. Hence the Lord says in the Gospel: [[Luke 11:41|that which remaineth, give alms: and behold, all things are clean unto you|Quod superest, date eleemosynam, et ecce omnia munda sunt vobis]]. And again: [[Luke 16:9|Make unto you friends of the mammon of iniquity: that when you shall fail, they may receive you into everlasting dwellings|Facite vobis amicos de mammona iniquitatis, ut quum defeceritis, recipiant vos in æterna tabernacula]]. [[4:12|Alms shall be a great confidence|Fiducia magna]], that is, a cause of great confidence, [[4:12|before the most high God|erit coram summo Deo]], alms both bodily and spiritual, [[4:12|to all them that give it|omnibus facientibus eam]]. For Christ declares that on the day of judgement he will judge by the works of mercy, and will say to the merciful: [[Matt 25:34|Come, ye blessed of my Father|Venite, benedicti Patris mei]], [[Matt 25:34|possess you the kingdom|percipite regnum]].

paras.t: Attende tibi ab omni fornicatione, tam simplici, quam adulterio, incestu, stupro, sacrilegio; a spirituali etiam fornicatione, præsertim ab idololatria. Et præter uxorem tuam, quam habiturus es, nunquam patiaris crimen scire, hoc est, nunquam alteri commiscearis, nec conscius tibi fias criminis tanti.
paras.en: [[4:13|Take heed to keep thyself, my son, from all fornication|Attende tibi ab omni fornicatione]], simple fornication as well as adultery[[Matt 5:27||]], incest, seduction, sacrilege; and from spiritual fornication too, above all from idolatry. [[4:13|and beside thy wife|Et præter uxorem tuam]], whom thou art to have, [[4:13|never endure to know a crime|nunquam patiaris crimen scire]], that is, never have intercourse with another, nor make thyself privy to so great a crime.

paras.t: Superbiam nunquam in tuo sensu interiori aut exteriori, aut in tuo verbo, imo nec facto, neque vestitu, nec aliquo apparatu, dominari permittas, ei consentiendo. Idcirco, si subrepat, mox reprime eam, et abjice tanquam diabolicum crimen, maledictionisque semen, et venenum mortiferum ac vitiorum originem, matrem, reginam. In ipsa enim initium sumpsit omnis perditio: quia per superbiam primus ille apostata angelus perdidit semetipsum, et angelos innumerabiles sibi attraxit; atque ex illa perditione consecuta et orta est invidia diaboli, per quam mors intravit in orbem terrarum, ut Sapiens disserit.
paras.en: [[4:14|Never suffer pride to reign in thy mind|Superbiam nunquam in tuo sensu]], inward or outward, [[4:14|or in thy words|aut in tuo verbo]], nay, nor in deed, nor in dress, nor in any display, by consenting to it. Therefore, if it creeps in, repress it at once, and cast it away as a devilish crime, the seed of malediction, a deadly poison, and the origin, mother and queen of the vices. [[4:14|for from it all perdition took its beginning|In ipsa enim initium sumpsit omnis perditio]]: because through pride that first apostate angel lost himself[[Is 14:4||]] [the margin gives Is. xiv, 4 and following; the fall of Lucifer is at Is 14:12], and drew innumerable angels after him; and from that perdition there followed and arose the envy of the devil, through which [[Wis 2:24|death came into the world|mors intravit in orbem terrarum]], as the Wise Man declares.

paras.t: Quicumque aliquid tibi operatus fuerit, statim ei mercedem restitue, præsertim si petit et egeat. Qui enim fraudem facit mercenario, et qui sanguinem fundit, fratres sunt, ut in Ecclesiastico legitur. Et merces mercenarii tui apud te omnino non remaneat, hoc est diutius quam licet. Nam et unum quatuor clamitantium vitiorum, est detentio mercedis operariorum, ut Jacobus asserit. Hinc Dominus in Levitico ait: Non morabitur opus mercenarii tui apud te usque mane. Communiter enim pauperes sunt operarii tales, et indigent sua mercede.
paras.en: [[4:15|If any man hath done any work for thee, immediately pay him his hire|Quicumque aliquid tibi operatus fuerit, statim ei mercedem restitue]], above all if he asks and is in need. For [[Ecclus 34:27|He that sheddeth blood, and he that defraudeth the laborer of his hire, are brothers|Qui enim fraudem facit mercenario, et qui sanguinem fundit, fratres sunt]], as is read in Ecclesiasticus [Denis names the two in the reverse order]. [[4:15|and let not the wages of thy hired servant stay with thee at all|Et merces mercenarii tui apud te omnino non remaneat]], that is, longer than is lawful. For the withholding of labourers' wages is one of the four vices that cry out [that is, the four sins crying to heaven for vengeance], as James asserts[[Jas 5:4||]]. Hence the Lord says in Leviticus: [[Lev 19:13|The wages of him that hath been hired by thee shall not abide with thee until the morning|Non morabitur opus mercenarii tui apud te usque mane]]. For such labourers are commonly poor, and need their wages.

paras.t: Quod ab alio oderis, hoc est, rationabiliter non vis, et abhorres, fieri tibi, vide ne tu aliquando alteri facias. Duo sunt præcepta juris naturalis, unum negativum obligans semper et ad semper, quod ponitur hic; aliud affirmativum, obligans semper, sed non ad semper, quod per Matthæum exprimit Christus: Omnia, inquiens, quæcumque vultis ut faciant vobis homines, ita et vos facite illis. Quorum unum in alio includitur.
paras.en: [[4:16|what thou wouldst hate|Quod ab alio oderis]], that is, what thou dost with reason not wish and dost abhor, [[4:16|to have done to thee by another|fieri tibi]], [[4:16|See thou never do to another|vide ne tu aliquando alteri facias]]. There are two precepts of the natural law: one negative, binding always and for always, which is set down here; the other affirmative, binding always but not for always [a negative precept binds at every moment; an affirmative one is always in force, but need not be acted on at every moment], which Christ expresses through Matthew: [[Matt 7:12|All things|Omnia]], he says, [[Matt 7:12|whatsoever you would that men should do to you, do you also to them|quæcumque vultis ut faciant vobis homines, ita et vos facite illis]]. Each of them is contained in the other.

paras.t: Panem tuum cum esurientibus et egenis comede: illos invitando ut tecum manducent, sicut sanctus Job fecit, qui ait: Si comedi buccellam meam solus, et non comedit pupillus ex ea. Hinc ait Unigenitus Dei: Quum facis prandium aut cœnam, noli vocare amicos tuos, neque fratres, neque cognatos, neque vicinos divites, ne forte et ipsi te reinvitent, et fiat tibi retributio; sed quum facis convivium, voca pauperes, debiles, claudos et cæcos, et beatus eris, quia non habent retribuere tibi. Retribuetur enim tibi in resurrectione justorum. Istud consilium est, non præceptum. Et de vestimentis tuis tibi superfluis nudos tege: quemadmodum beatissimus Joannes Baptista admonuit: Qui habet duas tunicas, det non habenti; et Isaias, Quum videris nudum, operi eum. Universa etenim misericordiæ opera tempore opportuno sunt adimplenda.
paras.en: [[4:17|Eat thy bread with the hungry and the needy|Panem tuum cum esurientibus et egenis comede]]: inviting them to eat with thee, as holy Job did, who says: [[Job 31:17|If I have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless hath not eaten thereof|Si comedi buccellam meam solus, et non comedit pupillus ex ea]]. Hence the Only-begotten of God says: [[Luke 14:12|When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends nor thy brethren nor thy kinsmen nor thy neighbours who are rich; lest perhaps they also invite thee again, and a recompense be made to thee|Quum facis prandium aut cœnam, noli vocare amicos tuos, neque fratres, neque cognatos, neque vicinos divites, ne forte et ipsi te reinvitent, et fiat tibi retributio]]; [[Luke 14:13|But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame and the blind|sed quum facis convivium, voca pauperes, debiles, claudos et cæcos]], [[Luke 14:14|And thou shalt be blessed, because they have not wherewith to make thee recompense: for recompense shall be made thee at the resurrection of the just|et beatus eris, quia non habent retribuere tibi. Retribuetur enim tibi in resurrectione justorum]]. This is a counsel, not a precept. [[4:17|and with thy garments|Et de vestimentis tuis]] that are more than thou needest [[4:17|cover the naked|nudos tege]]: as most blessed John the Baptist admonished, [[Luke 3:11|He that hath two coats, let him give to him that hath none|Qui habet duas tunicas, det non habenti]]; and Isaias, [[Is 58:7|when thou shalt see one naked, cover him|Quum videris nudum, operi eum]]. For all the works of mercy are to be fulfilled at the fitting time.

paras.t: Panem tuum et vinum tuum super sepulturam justi constitue, hoc est, in sepelitione fidelium refice pauperes bene pro spiritibus defunctorum in gratia. Non est autem erronee intelligendum, ut juxta quorumdam superstitionem, super monumenta mortuorum alimenta ponantur, quasi mortui corporalibus alimoniis egeant aut vescantur. De hoc recitat Augustinus in libro Confessionum, quemadmodum mater sua ad prædicationem Ambrosii, consuetudinem suam reliquerit: et quod iste sit sensus, apparet ex verbis sequentibus. Et noli ex eo manducare et bibere cum peccatoribus, hoc est incredulis, qui defunctis nequeunt suffragari.
paras.en: [[4:18|Lay out thy bread, and thy wine upon the burial of a just man|Panem tuum et vinum tuum super sepulturam justi constitue]], that is, at the burial of the faithful refresh the poor well, for the souls of those who have died in grace. It is not, however, to be wrongly understood, as though, after the superstition of some, food were to be set on the tombs of the dead, as if the dead needed or fed on bodily nourishment. Augustine tells of this in the book of the Confessions [book VI, chapter 2], how his mother gave up her custom at the preaching of Ambrose; and that this is the sense appears from the words that follow: [[4:18|and do not eat and drink thereof with the wicked|Et noli ex eo manducare et bibere cum peccatoribus]], that is, with unbelievers, who cannot help the dead by suffrages.

paras.t: Consilium semper a sapiente perquire, id est, diligenter inquire in arduis ac dubiis, in quibus ad expertorum, sapientium et Deum timentium est confugiendum consilium: quod etiam a sapientissimo Deo, et ex Scripturis ac patrum libris est inquirendum. Unde in Ecclesiastico docetur: Fili, sine consilio nihil facias, et post factum non pœnitebis.
paras.en: [[4:19|Seek counsel always of a wise man|Consilium semper a sapiente perquire]], that is, inquire diligently in hard and doubtful matters, in which one must have recourse to the counsel of the experienced, of the wise and of those who fear God; which is also to be sought from God, who is most wise, and from the Scriptures and the books of the Fathers. Hence it is taught in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 32:24|My son, do thou nothing without counsel, and thou shalt not repent when thou hast done|Fili, sine consilio nihil facias, et post factum non pœnitebis]].

paras.t: Omni tempore benedic Deum, laudando eum in prosperis et in adversis, perseveranter usque in finem, omni tempore opportuno, juxta illud in Psalmo: Benedicam Dominum in omni tempore, semper laus ejus in ore meo; et pete ab eo, ut vias, hoc est actiones tuas interiores exterioresque dirigat per se, per angelicam custodiam, per suos vicarios, atque per consiliarios bonos. Qua directione superna jugiter ac maxime indigemus, secundum illud Proverbiorum: Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Dei est dirigere gressus ejus. Unde sanctus ille ait Jeremias sanctificatus in utero: Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri est, ut ambulet et dirigat gressus suos. Ideo cum Psalmista oremus: Gressus meos dirige secundum eloquium tuum. Et omnia consilia tua in ipso permaneant, ita ut nullius consilio acquiescas contra Dei præcepta ac documenta. Cuncta quoque consilia quæ inquiris, finaliter ordines, ut Deo complaceas, et salveris.
paras.en: [[4:20|Bless God at all times|Omni tempore benedic Deum]], praising him in prosperity and in adversity, perseveringly unto the end, at every fitting time, according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 33:2|I will bless the Lord at all times, his praise shall be always in my mouth|Benedicam Dominum in omni tempore, semper laus ejus in ore meo]]; [[4:20|and desire of him to direct thy ways|et pete ab eo, ut vias]], that is, thy actions inward and outward, by himself, through the guardianship of the angels, through his vicars, and through good counsellors. Of this heavenly direction we stand continually and above all in need, according to that of Proverbs: [[Prov 16:9|The heart of man disposeth his way: but the Lord must direct his steps|Cor hominis disponit viam suam, sed Dei est dirigere gressus ejus]] [Denis reads *Dei*, of God, for *Domini*, the Lord]. Whence that holy Jeremias, who was sanctified in the womb, says: [[Jer 10:23|I know, O Lord, that the way of a man is not his: neither is it in a man to walk, and to direct his steps|Scio, Domine, quia non est hominis via ejus, nec viri est, ut ambulet et dirigat gressus suos]]. Therefore let us pray with the Psalmist: [[Ps 118:133|Direct my steps according to thy word|Gressus meos dirige secundum eloquium tuum]]. [[4:20|and that all thy counsels may abide in him|Et omnia consilia tua in ipso permaneant]], so that thou acquiesce in no one's counsel against the precepts and teachings of God. And order all the counsels thou seekest to this end, that thou mayest please God and be saved.

paras.t: Indico etiam tibi, fili mi, dedisse, hoc est concessisse, me decem talenta argenti Gabelo, etc., prout supra expositum est.
paras.en: [[4:21|I tell thee also, my son, that I lent|Indico etiam tibi, fili mi, dedisse]], that is, granted, [[4:21|ten talents of silver|me decem talenta argenti]] [[4:21|to Gabelus|Gabelo]], etc., as was explained above[[Tob 1:17||]] [the margin note here is illegible; the loan is told at Tob 1:17].

paras.t: Noli timere, fili mi, carnali, mundano, inordinato et turbulento timore. Pauperem quidem vitam gerimus in temporalibus, sed multa bona habebimus, hoc est copiosa charismata gratiæ in præsenti, bonaque gloriæ in futuro, si timuerimus Deum, filiali timore: juxta illud Psalmistæ, Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam nihil deest timentibus eum; et recesserimus ab omni peccato, præsertim mortali, et etiam veniali pro posse: a quibus potissime receditur corde, ea abhorrendo: et fecerimus bene […] duas quasi integrales partes justitiæ, Propheta dicente: Declina a malo, et fac bonum, etc.
paras.en: [[4:23|Fear not, my son|Noli timere, fili mi]], with a carnal, worldly, inordinate and turbulent fear. [[4:23|we lead indeed a poor life|Pauperem quidem vitam gerimus]] in temporal things, [[4:23|but we shall have many good things|sed multa bona habebimus]], that is, abundant gifts of grace in the present, and the goods of glory in the future, [[4:23|if we fear God|si timuerimus Deum]] with a filial fear, according to that of the Psalmist, [[Ps 33:10|Fear the Lord, all ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him|Timete Dominum, omnes sancti ejus, quoniam nihil deest timentibus eum]] [Denis reads *nihil deest*, nothing is lacking, for *non est inopia*]; [[4:23|and depart from all sin|et recesserimus ab omni peccato]], above all mortal sin, and venial too as far as we can: from which one departs chiefly in heart, by abhorring them; [[4:23|and do that which is good|et fecerimus bene]] […] the two integral parts, as it were, of justice, as the Prophet says: [[Ps 36:27|Decline from evil and do good|Declina a malo, et fac bonum]], etc.
